blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights the fascinating and concerning existence of adversarial perturbations—imperceptible changes to inputs that cause deep neural network classifiers to misclassify images. Unlike prior work focused on input-specific perturbations, this paper introduces a single universal perturbation that fools the vast majority of input images across a dataset. The author draws an analogy to 20th-century warfare camouflage, suggesting such perturbations could be used to deceive AI systems in future conflicts. The paper demonstrates that these perturbations are highly effective (fooling over 90% of images in some models) and generalize well across different architectures and datasets. The key insight is the discovery of a low-dimensional subspace that captures geometric correlations in the decision boundaries of classifiers, explaining why universal perturbations work and why they generalize so effectively. The author also explores whether fine-tuning can mitigate these vulnerabilities, finding only limited success.
paper_abstract: Face powder Given a state-of-the-art deep neural network classifier, we show the existence of a universal (image-agnostic) and very small perturbation vector that causes natural images to be misclassified with high probability. We propose a systematic algorithm for computing universal perturbations, and show that state-of-the-art deep neural networks are highly vulnerable to such perturbations, albeit being quasiimperceptible to the human eye. We further empirically analyze these universal perturbations and show, in particular, that they generalize very well across neural networks. The surprising existence of universal perturbations reveals important geometric correlations among the high-dimensional decision boundary of classifiers. It further outlines potential security breaches with the existence of single directions in the input space that adversaries can possibly exploit to break a classifier on most natural images.1 Joystick Chihuahua Chihuahua Jay Grille Labrador Thresher Labrador Flagpole Tibetan mastiff
